title: Amazon KDP is freezing self-publisher accounts and withholding royalties over automated Canva copyright flags
description: Amazon's Kindle Direct Publishing (KDP) has implemented an aggressive, automated copyright detection system that frequently targets books containing stock graphics from Canva. Self-publishers are waking up to frozen accounts and withheld royalties, given only 5 days to prove they hold commercial copyright licenses for the basic vectors they used. Because Canva's terms of service are notoriously muddy regarding 'print on demand' rights, publishers are losing entire income streams overnight.
the_opportunity: Build a 'KDP-Safe' vector asset library and generation tool specifically for low-content book publishers. It must provide absolute, cryptographically verifiable, one-click commercial licenses for every single asset downloaded. Alternatively, create an automated 'KDP License Defender' tool that generates instant, Amazon-compliant copyright verification PDFs that authors can submit the second their account gets flagged.
the_gap: The graphic design market treats all users the same, but the self-publishing market operates under the draconian, automated rules of Amazon KDP. There is a massive gap for a design tool that doesn't just provide graphics, but provides 'Amazon-proof legal immunity' along with them.
who_is_affected: Indie authors relying on KDP royalties
substitutes: Buying expensive exclusive rights from illustrators

sample_quotes.text: I just saw a video today of a young lady saying that Amazon KDP had frozen her account and all the money in it due to copywrite questions. She had only 5 days to send them proof that she had copywrites to her book or books or she could lose her account (and money)all together. She had used some Canva graphics or pictures and that was the problem. Yikes!
sample_quotes.author: @SCfanIam100

sample_quotes.text: They ruined the pricing for small teams. We are 3 people and the jump from free to the tier that actually gives us what we need is absurd. Looking for a fast markdown alternative that just works.
